en: The Liturgical Text for Prostrating and Repenting Before the Names of the Thirty-five Buddhas Spoken by the Buddha, in one fascicle;
excerpted from the *Upāliparipṛcchā-sūtra*. [Compiled by] the Grand Marshal of the Household, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial.

Translated by the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra, Tripitaka Master of Da Guangzhi Daxingshan Monastery, who was Duke of Sū, with a fief of three thousand households, invested with the purple robe, posthumously granted the title of Minister of Works, and conferred the honorific name Dajian (Great Mirror).
By Imperial Decree: *Namo* Śākyamuni Buddha. *Namo* Vajradṛḍhatejas-vināśana Buddha. *Namo* Ratnārcis Buddha.

Homage to the Buddha Ratnapadmavicitravyūhaśikhara-rāja. "May all such Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, who have appeared in all worlds throughout the ten directions, who abide and traverse the world, deign to observe me and take pity upon me."
Whether in this life or in other lives, since beginningless time, I have extensively committed various sins—whether acting myself, rejoicing in others' actions, or inciting others to act;
whether stealing the property of the Buddha or the property of the Sangha from the four quarters, whether acting myself, rejoicing in others' actions, or inciting others to act;
or whether committing the five crimes of immediate retribution and the ten unwholesome paths of action, whether acting myself, rejoicing in others' actions, or inciting others to act.

Due to these karmic obstructions, their bodies and minds are shrouded, causing them to be born within the eight difficult conditions; they may fall into the realms of hell, animals, or hungry ghosts; or be born in remote borderlands as Mlecchas; or be born in the long-lived heavens; or, even if they obtain a human body, their faculties are incomplete; or they give rise to false views that deny cause and effect; or they feel aversion toward the appearance of Buddhas in the world.

All such karmic obstructions, I now, before all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones—who possess all-knowledge, who possess the five eyes, who have realized the limit of reality, who are the weighers, the knowers, and the seers—sincerely confess in their entirety; I dare not conceal them. May my moral discipline and restraint be restored as they were before.

Furthermore, I pray that all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, will accept me, protect and mind me, and bear witness for me: whether in this life or in other lives throughout the beginningless past while wandering in saṃsāra, if I have ever given even a single morsel of food to an animal, or have ever observed a single pure precept, or have ever cultivated roots of goodness through the practice of brahmacarya, or have ever cultivated even a small portion of the roots of goodness of unsurpassed wisdom—may all these be gathered together, calculated, and weighed.
Just as all Buddhas of the three times, within their most supreme and unsurpassed prayers of dedication, vow that all shall be dedicated toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment:
"I confess all sins, rejoice in all merits, and entreat all Buddhas; may they realize unexcelled wisdom."
"The Buddhas of the past and future, And the Honored One among men in the present— To this ocean of immeasurable merit, I now prostrate in worship.

The above list of the names of the thirty-five Buddhas, together with the method for repentance, is extracted from the *Upāliparipṛcchā Sūtra*. It can purify heavy karmic obstructions and grave offenses; it enables one to fulfill all that is sought in this life, including meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), liberation (*vimukti*), and the various stages of the bodhisattva path (*bhūmi*).

The practitioners of the Mahāyāna throughout the five regions of India constantly perform the rite of repentance during the six periods of the day without fail. Although their merits are vast and numerous, they cannot be recorded in full for fear of excessive detail; here, I have briefly noted those practices as observed in India, while the remainder is as described in the original scripture. *The Liturgy of Repentance and the Names of the Thirty-five Buddhas Spoken by the Buddha*.
